newsitem.title: UK: Stocks rise in London, fall in Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: Stocks rise in London, fall in Tokyo.

text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended Thursday.

LONDON - Stocks finished mostly higher, but investors remained wary ahead of key economic indicators in the United States Friday and were still unsettled by Wednesday's unexpected British interest rate rise. The FTSE 100 index of blue-chip shares settled 15.2 points higher at 3,979.1, its peak for the day, after earlier slipping to its lowest level for a month.

FRANKFURT- The German DAX index of 30 leading shares ended thin-volume bourse trade at its lowest level in four weeks as the possibility of further German interest rate cuts faded and Wall Street closed lower. The DAX index closed floor dealings down 19.48 points, or 0.73 percent, at 2,659.25. In post bourse trade the DAX was up 6.68 at 2671.40.

PARIS - French shares closed higher before the All Saints holiday Friday with only the expiry of the October options contract in the late afternoon giving a sparkle to otherwise listless trading. The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 15.75 points or 0.74 percent at 2,140.51.

ZURICH - Swiss shares ended with minor gains on modest volumes after a quiet session marked by see-saw moves in the stock indices. Investors were likely to hedge their bets on Friday ahead of U.S. employment figures and due to the fact that some markets such as those in Germany will remain closed for All Saints' Day. The blue-chip Swiss Market Index rose 2.2 points, to 3,725.3. The broad Swiss Performance Index (SPI) added 2.73 points, to 2,394.05 points.

TOKYO - Tokyo's key benchmark, the Nikkei 225, closed beneath 20,500 points for the first time since Sept. 12. Most investors were sidelined, with futures-linked selling weighing heavily on the average. The Nikkei average fell 214.81 points or 1.04 percent to 20,466.86.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks ended stronger after see-sawing in a wide range, caught between optimism after Wednesday's surge in prices and caution ahead of the release of fresh U.S. economic data. The Hang Seng index rose 72.09 points to 12,477.56 after slipping into negative territory early in the session to a low of 12,377.88 and rising to an afternoon high of 12,496.57.

SYDNEY - Australian shares closed firmer after a late buying spree spruced up an otherwise lifeless session as investors contemplated the future direction of local interest rates. The benchmark All Ordinaries index closed 13.5 points higher at 2,350.2, well off its intra-session low of 2,329.3.

JOHANNESBURG - South African industrial shares ended firm buoyed by a firmer currency and golds were firm despite a weak bullion price and a softer rand gold price. The overall index ended up 83.5 points to 6,975.3 points, the industrial index gained 84.5 points to 8,209.2 points and the gold index rose 24.2 points to 1,732.3.
